title: Understanding N-gram Limitations
text: Consider how N-grams capture sequences. They don't account for the biological significance of codons, which are specific sequences of three consecutive letters.

title: Non-consecutive Segments
text: N-grams can mistakenly capture non-consecutive sequences as valid segments, which is not biologically meaningful in DNA analysis.

title: Meaningless Short Segments
text: Segments with $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters don't correspond to any meaningful biological unit, yet N-grams would treat them as valid features.

title: Overlapping Segments
text: N-grams can create overlapping segments, which might not align with the distinct codon structure in DNA.

title: Wrap-around Segments
text: DNA sequences don't wrap around, but N-grams might capture segments as if they do, leading to incorrect feature representation.
